key_findings: VP cholinergic neurons receive functional monosynaptic glutamatergic input from STN CaMKII neurons; optogenetic stimulation of the STNGlu-VP projection reduces mechanical thresholds, which is attenuated by chemogenetic inhibition of VP cholinergic neurons.
VP cholinergic neurons are the major source of pain-evoked ACh release in the VP, and ACh release is enhanced in SNI mice.
α4 and α7 nAChRs are the major functional nAChRs in VP cholinergic, GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons; their activation in the VP causes mechanical (and for α4 thermal) hypersensitivity.
In SNI, Chrna4 is upregulated in VP GABAergic neurons and downregulated in VP glutamatergic neurons; Chrna7 is reduced in cholinergic and glutamatergic neurons.
SNI causes hyperexcitability of VP GABAergic neurons and hypoactivity of VP glutamatergic neurons.
shRNA knockdown of α4 nAChR in VP GABAergic neurons attenuates hyperalgesia in neuropathic pain.
